Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on Surah 110, verses 1–3:

﴿When the help of God and the conquest come﴾. By "the conquest" is meant the conquest of Makkah, al-Ta'if, and the other lands that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) conquered. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The help is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyya, and the conquest is the conquest of Makkah." It was also said: "The help is the conversion to Islam of the people of Yemen." The announcement of all of this before it occurred is a report of the unseen, and so it is one of the signs of prophethood. ﴿And you see the people entering the religion of God in multitudes﴾, that is, in groups. This is because a great number embraced Islam after the conquest of Makkah. It is related that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had with him ten thousand at the conquest of Makkah, and he had with him seventy thousand at the expedition of Tabuk. Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not die while there was a single disbelieving man among the Arabs." It has also been said that the number of Muslims at his death was one hundred and fourteen thousand, or even more.

﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness﴾. The glorification and the seeking of forgiveness have been mentioned, and the meaning of "with the praise of your Lord" has been explained earlier. If it is asked: "Why did God command him to glorify, to praise, and to seek forgiveness upon seeing the help and the conquest, and as his term drew near?" The answer is: He commanded him to glorify and praise as a thanksgiving for the help, the conquest, and the manifestation of Islam. He commanded him to do that, and to seek forgiveness as his term drew near, so that this would be provision for the Hereafter and preparation for meeting God.
